youtube.title: Deepwater Horizon Failed a Safety Test Hours Before It Exploded
youtube.description:
On April 20, 2010, the crew of the Deepwater Horizon ran a negative pressure test to check the cement sealing BP's Macondo well. The readings showed the well was not sealed, but supervisors accepted an explanation investigators later called "facially implausible" and declared the test a success. That night the well blew out; the explosion killed 11 workers and oil flowed into the Gulf of Mexico for 87 days. The presidential commission called the misread test a major contributing factor.

📂 Case File #055: Deepwater Horizon

Sources: National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill, Chief Counsel's Report (2011), via Phys.org https://phys.org/news/2011-02-bp-blowout.html ; Oil & Gas Journal, "Several immediate causes contributed to Macondo blowout" https://www.ogj.com/drilling-production/drilling-operations/article/17212806/several-immediate-causes-contributed-to-macondo-blowout
